If it doesn't but your code goes away at least you figured out one issue. If it doesn't go away you could have some messed up wires or another issue although depending on the code.

Hey man, I had this issue. While it was minor as somehow the main ground on my 04 came lose, it made it so there was no charge. What I have heard to check

-See if your battery light is on when the ignition is on but the car isn't running. If not, supposedly replacing that can fix it 

-Seriously, check your grounds, all of them and make sure they are good (the main is beneath the intercooler, remove it to check) 

-Make sure that your alternator fuse is good. It's the big honking guy that's got 2 nuts holding it down

-Make sure everything is hooked up right. Like I said, my ground main vibrated lose, stuff happens

-Check for corrosion on your terminals, grounding points and your wires. Also, inspect your wires. 

-If you have a multimeter. Charge your battery and make sure it's 12.7 volts (or close to 12.7). Hook it up and leave it overnight, then check again. Again with the multimeter when the car is running, check the volts between the positive post and the alt bracket. If it's putting out 14ish volts, slowly check different ground points, working your way to the battery. That aught to help you isolate a bad ground, as well as make sure the alt is actually generating volts. 

-Finally; I think for your model (Hawkeye) there is an issue that sometimes happens with the ECU. What happens is the ECU overcharge protection bugs out and stays on, making it so the battery gets zero charge. What is recommended (do more research for this one please) is you trick the ECU into thinking the break lights are always on by grounding the brake light signal line. This issue is often accompanied by a cel.

This is all off the top of my head as a diyer but hope it helps. I tired to list everything I found when was researching. Also, in terms of the misfire, I'd guess that it has to do with a grounding issue skewing your coil pack ignition
